I've used their services several times before (cat sterilization), and they've been excellent, with small incisions. However, I've never used their other services. On March 12, 1969, I tried their services for the first time (a stray cat gave birth).
I took her to this hospital because of my trust in them, despite having been to many other clinics before. Upon arrival, I informed the counter as usual,
that I wanted them to check if any kittens were left and if the kittens were healthy and had a chance of survival.

When it was time, an assistant took the mother cat for an X-ray.
Less than 5 minutes later, the doctor came out and said there were no bones in the film, meaning none were left. But they didn't check the kittens, even though I had informed the counter staff beforehand. I felt upset and neglected, like my precious lives weren't valued.

I already reported this, but the clinic is asking me to pay for a new checkup and vet fees again.

October 8, 2022. Today wasn't good at all. I'm a regular customer and have brought my cats here for vaccinations many times, but this time was very disappointing. 👺 Here's what happened: At 4 PM today, I brought four cats for vaccinations. I paid 1,490 baht by credit card, but the clinic didn't issue a receipt, only a slip for the next appointment. My partner asked for a receipt, and the clinic said we had to wait because they issue receipts for each cat individually. My partner waited. When the receipt came, one cat was overcharged by 330 baht. The clinic refunded the extra 330 baht in cash. Whether this was intentional or not, the clinic owner can check the CCTV footage. It's strange that they didn't issue a receipt in the first place; they've always provided them before. I urge other animal lovers to double-check their payments. **P.S. The cash refund wasn't complete either; it was 20 baht short. The person next to me also confirmed it.** 🧐 End of comment.

I called to make an appointment for a cat bath three days in advance. When I dropped off the cat at the appointed time at 10:00 AM, I was told to pick it up in the afternoon, but didn't say what time. I was running errands until 1:30 PM, and I didn't hear back. When I finished, I happened to be driving by and asked if the cats had been bathed. It turned out that none of them had been bathed, and they were still locked in the same basket they were brought in. I don't know if they'd eaten or drunk any food. I asked if they'd be able to bathe, but they said to come pick me up in the evening, and I don't know what time. Does bathing take all day? I agreed to bring them more than 10 kilometers from home for bathing. There are plenty of places closer to home because I expected it to be good. Personally, I really dislike this place. The male staff member had a grumpy, sullen expression, as if I were begging for service. When I brought my dog ​​for treatment, I asked the hospital to give him the day's medication, but the staff …

The doctor just prescribed medication and sent us home. The sign says "24" (like a house), but they're actually only open from 7 or 8 am to midnight. Think carefully before considering this hospital. The doctor prolongs the illness, and you'll waste a lot of money. Go to another clinic instead; it's more complete, faster, and safer.
The service from the cashier at Lanna Hospital wasn't great. She was stiff, had a cold, harsh tone, and seemed stern. In this case, we were taking our cat to be spayed, but we wanted a blood test first because she was sick and admitted to the hospital when she was younger.
The first blood test took several hours to get the results and cost over 2,000 baht. The doctor said her blood test results weren't good and she needed medication. We had to pick her up in 2-3 days and pay another 1,000+ baht.
The second blood test was also bad, so we had to pay again and pay for the medication again in 2-3 days.
The third blood test, which was delayed for a while because we were out of town, cost another 1,000 baht. The result was still bad. We asked the doctor if we could spay her right away, but the doctor insisted, no matter what, that we couldn't spay her because of the blood test results. So we asked to think about it first.
A few days later, we decided to go to another well-known clinic, one starting with the letter T. We've used this clinic many times before; the service is good, the doctors are friendly and they love animals. To get to the point, we took our cat for a blood test at the T. clinic, and the doctor was very kind and explained things nicely. She said that the kidney and platelet counts were slightly lower than normal, but it wouldn't affect the spaying procedure. It could be done without affecting our cat's life.
So we decided to go ahead with it, trusting the doctor, and took our cat. In short, our cat was spayed successfully. It's been several months now.
